text:
Noah: Heads-up — user reported confusing saved queries in Console when switching between route view and model view. They expected queries scoped to the model to show up when they clicked the model name, but Console kept offering only route-scoped ones.

Priya: that's an important UX hole. We currently treat savedqueries as route-first. We do have a "scope" field internally (team/route/global) but not model.

Ilya: quick product Q: when a user is viewing a model from the route page (e.g., /routes/chat -> model/redwood-lite), should the context automatically become model-scoped? Or should we keep the context pinned to route and let user opt-in to model scope?

Zoe (Design): my draft: default context stays route-scoped (to avoid surprise), but add a small context chip next to the model name: "Context: Route (change)". Clicking it opens a mini-menu: Route / Model / Team / Global. Selecting Model switches savedquery suggestions and applies model-specific telemetry filters.

Noah: sounds good. Also: when model switching happens because of fallback, we should show a subtle inline note: "Actual served model differs from configured model" and offer a one-click "view by served model" that applies the model scope and switches cost-preview.

Priya: backend impact: savedquery lookup endpoint is /api/savedqueries?route_id=XXX. We'll need to add support for model_id and a precedence order param. Evan, thoughts on perf?

Evan (Backend): adding model_id param is trivial. The tricky part is precedence merging: we need to return a ranked list (model-scoped first then route then team). Current response is a flat array; ranking would be OK but might need a new DB index. If we add model_id to the saved_queries table (nullable) and index (route_id, model_id), lookups should be fine. Migration is simple but will require write-path changes in SDKs.

Ilya: telemetry + sampling: if user switches to model scope we must align the telemetry time series to the model attribution sampling stream. Right now cost-preview aggregates by route only. Leo (Eng-ML) should weigh in on whether serve attribution history is available for the same retention window.

ConsoleBot: [note] rollout v2.9.0: savedqueries-search added (canary). Docs: https://docs.redwood/savedqueries-search

Zoe (Design): small UX ask: when switching scopes we should preserve any search/filter the user had in the query builder so they don't lose context. Also, show a pill "scope: model:redwood-lite" so it's clear.

Rashmi: edgecase: multi-route savedqueries (a view saved across multiple routes) — when in model scope we should show them but mark them as "multi-route" and surface which routes they apply to.

Noah: another edgecase: time window mismatch — savedqueries have been validated against sample data from the validation window (usually aligned with route intent). If model served=canary, the coverage might be low. Add a tiny warning: "This query's validation sample had <X% coverage for this model".

Evan (Backend): agree. We'll need to store validation metadata on savedqueries (last_validated_models and coverage_pct). That's a new column but small. Backfill can be done lazily on first open.

Ilya: quotas & cost-preview: currently cost-preview assumes current pin. If user switches scope to model that was actually served, cost-preview should recompute using model-specific per-token rates and quantization profile. That means cost-preview needs model_id param.

Priya: does any existing savedquery reference a model explicitly? We might also let users tag savedqueries with "model-intent" during creation to make this explicit.

Zoe (Design): UI flow: create-savedquery modal gets an optional "Associated model (optional)" dropdown (autofill from route models). If filled, we show a badge on the savedquery in lists. Keep it optional to avoid clutter.

Noah: action items: 1) API: add model_id and precedence param to savedqueries search (Evan + Ilya) 2) DB: add model_id nullable + validation metadata (Evan) 3) Console UI: scope chip + preserve search on switch + coverage warning (Zoe + Noah) 4) Telemetry: expose serve-attribution stream and per-model cost rates to cost-preview (Ilya + Eng-ML) 5) Docs + SDK flag for new param (Priya)

Evan (Backend): I'll open RFC for DB changes and include backfill plan (lazy update on read). Also will include sample query for (route_id, model_id, team_id) index.

Priya: I'll draft SDK changes and versioning notes — keep old API working (fallback to route-only behavior) until Console flips flag.

Noah: timeline? Can we get a small MVP (scope chip + model param support) in 3 sprints?

Zoe (Design): I can deliver lo-fi mocks and a small interactive prototype in 1 sprint.

Ilya: Eng-ML needs ~2 sprints to expose attribution streams and per-model cost lookup API. After that cost-preview can consume it.

Noah: ok. Let's treat this as an incremental rollout: 1) read-only model scope in Console (no savedquery creation changes) + API param accepted but not required, 2) allow tagging savedqueries in modal + migration.

ConsoleBot: [deploy] v2.9.0 canary updated with savedqueries-search endpoint at 5%: https://ci.example/redwood/console/1301

Noah: great — thanks everyone. Drop any multi-route or tenant aliasing corner cases here. We'll sync up in next weekly product review.

Zoe (Design): adding comment: include microcopy for "coverage" that explains how coverage is computed (sampled requests in last 24h that matched model attribution).

Priya: noted. Closing thread for now. :v:
